clue.text: Streamlined dairy came on post-restructure

indicators.note: after a restructure the letters of the preceding words have been rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A dairy's milk delivery arrived after the business was reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post-restructure' signals that DAIRY CAME ON is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodynamic shape is smooth and designed to slip through air, which is what streamlined describes.

clue.text: A locum tucking into teetotal shot

indicators.note: tucking into says the locum's word goes inside the abbreviation for teetotal

parts.note: a locum is a temporary stand-in, a temp

explanation.surface: A stand-in doctor sips a drink at a dry event.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a shot at something is to make an attempt, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Note Russian fighter is on speed in Settle again

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
rate means speed, as in 'at a great rate'

explanation.surface: A Russian jet speeds over the Yorkshire town of Settle, a musical note sounding.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is also a market town in North Yorkshire, which the capital letter exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: To remigrate is to move to and set up home in a place again, that is to resettle.

clue.text: Smoke methamphetamine under Dutch railway

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places this piece below the others

parts.note: ice is slang for crystal methamphetamine

explanation.surface: Someone uses crystal meth beneath a Dutch railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry ice gives off a dense white vapour used for stage fog, so it makes smoke effects.

clue.text: Mindless decisions of nob in rear hurt SAS at front

indicators.note: hurt means damaged, so these letters are broken up and rearranged
at front picks only the opening letter of SAS

explanation.surface: A toff's injured backside is the subject, with elite soldiers leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurt' rearranges IN REAR into RAINER, after NOB as written. 'of' is a link; SAS is the British special forces regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is a choice so obvious that it needs no thought at all.

clue.text: Dude getting rude ultimately causes shock

parts.note: dude is slang for a man

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of rude

explanation.surface: A man's rudeness ends up startling people.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick mass of it, and a mane is a thick head of hair.

clue.text: Wag seen with lag all over the papers and TV?

indicators.note: all over means the convict's word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: an old lag is a convict, a con
newspapers and television together are the media

explanation.surface: A joker turns up next to a convict who is splashed across newspapers and television.
explanation.definitionFit: A wag is a habitual joker, and a comedian is someone who jokes for a living.

clue.text: Couple of grams American snorted … crack?

indicators.note: snorted means taken in, so the letter for American goes inside the pair

parts.note: g is the abbreviation for gram, and a couple of them is GG

explanation.surface: An American snorts two grams of drugs, then crack is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug picture is a decoy: crack here means a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty remark, and a gag is a joke, so both nouns name a quip.

clue.text: Good girl in The Mirror?

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A well-behaved girl appears in the tabloid newspaper The Mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper; here it just means a looking-glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass, as in looking-glass, is an old word for a mirror.

clue.text: Flatulence kills folk unable to shut traps!

parts.note: gas is a word for flatulence
a hunter bags game, so bags means kills

explanation.surface: Wind is so lethal that it finishes off people who never stop talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is slang for a mouth; gasbags are chatterers who never close theirs.

clue.text: English soldier gets millions in fiddle

indicators.note: in places the letter for millions inside the word for fiddle

parts.note: to toy with something is to fiddle with it
M is a million, so two of them, MM, stand for millions

explanation.surface: A British soldier is paid millions through some fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy, from Tommy Atkins, is the traditional nickname for a private in the British Army.

clue.text: Times numbers around average? Not at all!

parts.note: times as in multiplication, read 'by' (three by four)

indicators.note: around means the word for numbers goes about the word for average

parts.note: the mean is an average

explanation.surface: Is a times-table answer near the average? Absolutely not.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom by no means is an emphatic denial, just as not at all is.

clue.text: Master criminal aiming a carbine at head

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so these letters are twisted into a new order
at head picks only the first letter of carbine

explanation.surface: A criminal mastermind points a rifle at someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges AIMING A with the C from 'carbine at head'.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician is an expert so skilled they seem to work wonders, so a master of a craft.

clue.text: Take too much flipping dope, ecstasy and port

parts.note: OD is short for overdose

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the fool and the drug are read backwards

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone overdoses on drugs and ecstasy, flipping out in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns ASS + E round to give ESSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Main Cameron policy "by egoistic fools"

indicators.note: fools, as a verb, means tricks, so these letters are messed about

explanation.surface: A sneer that David Cameron's flagship policy was devised by vain idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fools' rearranges BY EGOISTIC. David Cameron was UK Prime Minister 2010-16.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Society was the flagship idea of David Cameron's 2010 Conservative manifesto.

clue.text: The thing I just said's rubbish, husband admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the letter for husband goes inside

parts.note: tat means cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A spouse confesses that what was just said is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: The demonstrative pronoun that points back to a remark just made.

clue.text: People like me cause inns to be smashed up

indicators.note: smashed up means wrecked, so these letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A hooligan admits that types like them get pubs wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed up' rearranges CAUSE INNS. The setter cheerfully casts themself as a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter is joking that those who annoy, as they do, are pests.

clue.text: Cold in the extreme? Cold and peaky in the extreme!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the most peaky country, with the most peaks, is the hilliest

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about extreme cold is answered with talk of being very cold and peaky.
explanation.walkthrough: Peaky usually means looking pale and unwell; here it means full of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilly means cold, and its superlative names the coldest degree of chill.

clue.text: Issue rebuked soldiers brought about Latin navy

indicators.note: brought about means placed around, so the letter for Latin is enclosed

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Scolded soldiers are made to sail around in a Latin navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the legal sense means offspring, so a person's children.

clue.text: Weapons for some in a rut said costly instruments

definitions.text: Weapons for some in a rut

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: costly means dear and the instruments are horns

explanation.surface: Pricey musical instruments are said to be the weapons of creatures in a rut.
explanation.walkthrough: A rut here is the mating season, when stags fight with their antlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stags lock antlers in the breeding season, so antlers serve rutting males as weapons.

clue.text: Take away budgie smugglers or pump for answers?

parts.note: the prefix de- means removing or taking away, as in de-ice
budgie smugglers is Australian slang for tight swimming briefs

explanation.surface: Should one strip off someone's tight trunks or grill them for information?
explanation.definitionFit: Debriefing is questioning someone in detail about a task they have completed.

clue.text: Fancy I must open large barrel, wanting gallon

indicators.note: must open means the letter I goes into the remaining letters
wanting means lacking, so the gallon letter is removed

parts.note: a keg is a small barrel

explanation.surface: Someone has to crack open a big barrel, short of a gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' strips G from KEG, leaving KE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to like it, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Royal suggestive about knight's tendency to sin?

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for royalty

indicators.note: about means the word for suggestive goes round the knight's letter

parts.note: racy means risqué or suggestive
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A royal's risqué remarks about a knight hint at sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Errancy is the state of erring, straying from what is right, hence a leaning toward wrongdoing.

clue.text: One making barrels of cash primarily loves a …

indicators.note: primarily picks only the opening letter of cash

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O, and two of them are OO
a means per, as in 'ten pounds a head'

explanation.surface: Someone making barrels of money mostly loves... the sentence runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 23 Down, a split surface. 'barrels of cash' wants to be wealth; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooper is a craftsman who makes and repairs wooden casks.

clue.text: Courage and what one might find it in?

definitions.meaning: British slang for nerve or courage

definitions.text: what one might find it in?
definitions.meaning: 'it' is gin and it from 29 Across, or any drink

explanation.surface: Is courage the thing, and where would one look for it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' meaning courage is British slang ("lost his bottle"). Dutch courage is drink, found in a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle as a noun means nerve, and drink comes in a bottle.

clue.text: … gem tense old man smuggled into Australia

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: smuggled into puts the father's word inside the nickname for Australia

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia
old man is slang for father, PA

explanation.surface: A nervous father smuggles a gemstone into Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 21 Down: a cooper loves a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a precious stone, usually yellow, so it is a gem.

clue.text: Some 'disc roll errors' in down browser?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A web user scrolling down meets some glitches on a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reads a page by moving it down the screen scrolls, so they are a scroller.

clue.text: Stand out around statesmen at summit as moral

indicators.note: around means the word for stand out goes about the chosen letter

parts.note: to jut is to stand out or project

indicators.note: at summit picks the top letter of statesmen in this down clue

explanation.surface: Political leaders at a summit are urged to stand out as upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Just describes conduct that is right and fair, so ethically sound, which is moral.

clue.text: Harry Hoskins' left a Parisian to get drug

parts.note: Hoskins is the setter, so Hoskins is becomes I'm
port is the left side of a ship
un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: The setter goes off with a Frenchman to buy drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoskins is the setter, so 'Hoskins'' is read as 'Hoskins is', that is I'M. 'to get' is a link. Harry here is the verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester them persistently, and to importune is to pester with repeated demands.

clue.text: Writer grabbing hold of engineers in Pride

indicators.note: grabbing hold of means the pen holds the engineers' letters inside

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool
RE stands for the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: An author takes hold of engineers at a Pride parade.
explanation.definitionFit: To pride oneself on something is to preen oneself, both verbs of self-congratulation.

clue.text: Fine Happy Mondays dancer out of his head in city abroad

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: out of his head means losing his head, the first letter

parts.note: Bez was the maraca-shaking dancer of the Manchester band Happy Mondays

explanation.surface: A fine-looking dancer from Happy Mondays is off his head somewhere overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of his head' also means intoxicated, apt for Bez.
explanation.definitionFit: Fez is a historic city in Morocco, so a city abroad for a British setter.

clue.text: Try gin and it mixed by tenor: extremely tasty substance?

indicators.note: mixed suggests a cocktail being stirred, so these letters are rearranged
extremely picks the outermost letters of tasty

explanation.surface: A cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth with a tenor is, at the edges, tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin and it' is a real cocktail, but 'and' here is only a link and stays out of the anagram that 'mixed' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The nitty-gritty is the essential core of a matter, its real substance.
